Your first working screen is ready. Open it here:

**http://maker:4001**

You'll see an empty bookmark list with a box at the top for pasting a link.

**Please try this one action:** paste a link into the box and press **Save**. If you want a realistic-looking result, try something like `https://www.nytimes.com/article` or `arstechnica.com` — but any web address will work. Watch what happens to the item that appears in your list below.

A couple of things I decided on my own for this first screen — please tell me if they feel right:

- **What each saved link shows:** I chose to display the auto-filled **title**, the **site name and web address**, a short **description**, and **when you saved it**. That's my guess at the "basic details" you meant — let me know if something's missing or unnecessary.
- **How details get filled in:** in the real app these would be pulled from the page itself; here in this preview I'm *simulating* that lookup, so a few well-known sites return rich details and others get a best-guess title. The behaviour to judge is "details appear automatically without you typing them" — not the exact text.
- **Layout:** a single top-to-bottom list, newest link first.

Once you've saved a link or two, tell me how that felt — especially whether saving was quick enough and whether the auto-filled details are the right ones.
